title: Jeffrey Buckley, PhD
text:
I am a Lecturer in Research Pedagogy in the Faculty of Engineering and Technology at Technological University of the Shannon: Midlands Midwest and Visiting Senior Lecturer in Technology Education in the Department of Behavioural Sciences and Learning at Linköping University. I am the Editor-in-Chief of the International Journal of Technology and Design Education and the Series Editor for the Emergent Directions in Engineering Education book series, both published by Springer Nature. I am also an Associate Editor for the European Journal of Engineering Education, an Advisory Board Member for Educare, and an Editorial Board Member for Educational Psychology Review, SN Social Sciences, and The Educational and Developmental Psychologist. I received my PhD in education and communication in the technical sciences from KTH Royal Institute of Technology in 2018.
I study and conduct research broadly in technology and engineering education, but am particularly interested in the role of spatial ability in learning, the use of adaptive comparative judgement in educational assessment, and conducting meta-research with the aim of improving research practices broadly within technology and engineering education research. You can read more about my research interests here.
I teach modules in Research Methodology, Academic Writing, and Research Ethics to Doctoral and Masters students in Faculties of Engineering, Science, the Social Sciences, and Art and Design, and am generally interested in supporting postgraduate students and early career academics in their research journeys.

title: My Research Programme
text:
My research programme is concerned with how education can better support meaningful learning, authentic assessment, and trustworthy knowledge generation, with a particular emphasis on technology and engineering education.
I study spatial ability because formal education often focuses most directly on disciplinary competence, while cognitive factors that may shape learning and performance receive less sustained attention. Spatial ability has been linked to achievement in STEM, including specifically in technology and engineering contexts, in ways that suggest it may play an important role in students’ educational experiences. Understanding that role more clearly may help make education more supportive, efficient, and equitable.
I study assessment and comparative judgement because assessment mechanisms influence pedagogy. When assessment is aligned with the aims of a subject, it can support more authentic forms of activity and engagement. I see Adaptive Comparative Judgement as a promising approach for the assessment of complex and open-ended performance, and I am interested in how better designed and more accessible ACJ systems might contribute to better educational practice.
I conduct meta-research because educational improvement depends on the quality of the knowledge base that informs it. Through editorial and research work, I regularly encounter studies constrained by validity issues or methodological limitations, to the point of reducing their usefulness to the field. Strengthening research practices can improve knowledge generation in general, which in turn can better support educational practice.
These interests come together in an integrated research programme organised around three intersecting pillars as shown below.




Research Pillars




Learning and Spatial Ability
Focuses on the role of spatial ability in learning, development, and performance in technology and engineering education.
View my related publications

Current Interests


Spatial ability development through intervention
Understanding the structure and interrelationships of spatial factors
Associations between spatial ability and learning





Assessment and Comparative Judgement
Focuses on the use of adaptive comparative judgement for the assessment of complex competencies, typically design.
View my related publications

Current Interests


The development of ACJ systems
The valid assessment of design activity
Non-educational measurement applications of ACJ





Research Credibility and Meta-research
Focuses on the improvement of research practices in technology and engineering education.
View my related publications

Current Interests


Improving replicability in technology and engineering education research
Examining research robustness, reproducibility, and transparency
Conducting evidence synthesis and meta-scientific critique





Research Intersections
While the pillars above represent distinct domains, my work actively engages them in an interdisciplinary way.




Spatial ability × Assessment

Can spatial ability be recognised and evaluated in authentic assessment contexts?





Spatial ability × Meta-research

How can we improve validity in spatial ability measurement?





Comparative Judgement × Meta-research

How can we systematically evaluate and validate the theoretical claims underpinning comparative judgement?

title: Teaching
text:
I coordinate and lecture across the following modules. Below, you can access up to date teaching materials for each.





Research Ethics
RES09073 | Technological University of the Shannon: Midlands Midwest
Critically reflect on research practices, from questionable research practices and open science, to informed consent and ethical philosophies.
 View Materials








Academic Writing
RES09074 | Technological University of the Shannon: Midlands Midwest
Explore the academic publishing landscape from structuring empirical manuscripts and research theses, through critiquing the peer review process and developing research impact statements.
 View Materials








Research Methodology
RES09075 | Technological University of the Shannon: Midlands Midwest
Develop a broad understanding of research methodology, considering research paradigms, methodological alignment, theories on the nature of knowledge, research credibility, and common quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods designs.
 View Materials








Statistical Literacy and Reproducible Analysis
RES09085 | Technological University of the Shannon: Midlands Midwest
Understand the importance of statistical literacy and reproducibility in quantitative research, and develop skills to critically evaluate statistical analyses and promote reproducibility in your own research.
 View Materials








Contemporary Methodologies in STEM Education Research
Linköping University
Explore contemporary methodologies in STEM education research with a focus on methodological alignment, research credibility, and practical implementation.
 View Materials
